subject: only children
one_liner: Local reviews written exclusively by people who have never had to share a back seat, a bedroom, or the last dumpling.
brand_voice_notes: Earnest local-reviews platform run by and for only children. Every rating is really a rating of how much attention the reviewer personally received, and the brand treats that as a rigorous methodology. Confident, slightly wounded, never self-aware. Uses the words 'verified', 'sole' and 'undivided' as trust signals.

hero.h1: Every place in town, rated by the only person who mattered.
hero.sub: Party of One is a review platform written exclusively by only children. 41,200 verified reviewers, zero siblings, and every star reflects how much attention the reviewer personally received.

features.title: Sibling-Free Verified
features.blurb: Every reviewer uploads a notarized family tree before posting. Half-siblings trigger a manual audit. Cousins are permitted but disclosed at the bottom of the review in smaller type.

features.title: The Adult Table Index
features.blurb: Venues are scored on how quickly a nine-year-old gets seated with the grown-ups and asked for their opinion on the regional housing market. The current city leader is a tapas bar that closed in March.

features.title: Last Dumpling Guarantee
features.blurb: We only list restaurants where shared plates arrive in quantities divisible by one. Family-style dining has been delisted pending an appeal we do not intend to hear.

testimonials.quote: I gave Olive Garden one star because the server addressed the whole table. I was the table.

demo_screen_concept: A Yelp-style search results screen for 'places that won't make me share'. Category tabs (Restaurants, Family Gatherings, Road Trips, Birthday Parties), filter chips (Sibling-free, Adult Table, Single portions, Parents reachable), a sort control, and a list of listing cards: star ratings as gold reward-chart stickers, an 'Attention Received' meter, the Adult Table Index, a price level, and a snippet from a top review. A featured 'Reviewer's Choice' listing sits on top with a photo. Clicking a card opens a detail drawer with three full reviews and a write-a-review form with a sticker star picker that posts the review to the top of the list, because of course it does.

design_direction.style: Primary-school reward chart, classroom daylight mode. The page is staged as a grade-school star chart and handwriting worksheet kept by a very attentive teacher for a class of exactly one student: pale newsprint ruled with blue handwriting lines and a dashed red midline, gold and red foil reward stickers for every rating, and red-pen teacher marks (circles, ticks, 'see me') on anything that needs attention. One light mode only. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: large-print sliders and highlighter swipes, headshot glossies, staples, applause signs, SMPTE bars, pegboard, aisle signs, shelf tags, cork, push pins, tape strips, bites, pulp cells, grade stamps, vent holes, vinyl bladders, valves, weld seams, chenille, brass plates. Also absent: glassmorphism, blur, neon, dark mode, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The ruled worksheet: sections sit on #FBF8F0 newsprint with repeating 32px blue #B9C6E4 baselines and a dashed red #E8A39D midline, and a single vertical red margin rule 56px from the left edge. (2) The reward sticker: every star rating, tier mark and badge is a scalloped-edge circle sticker in gold #F2B01E or red #D2342B with a white inner ring and a slight 2deg rotation, like a teacher stuck it on. (3) The red pen: primary CTA underlines, the highlighted tier and the 'Reviewer's Choice' tag get a hand-drawn SVG red ellipse or tick, stroke 2.5px, never more than one per card. (4) The index card: cards are white #FFFFFF with 3px radius, a 1px #D9D2C0 edge, a thin blue header rule and a hard 3px 3px 0 shadow in #1E2A4A at 12 percent. Headings are Young Serif, sentence case. Body is Figtree 17px/1.62. Every rating, count and price is Red Hat Mono with tabular figures.
design_direction.archetype: Marketplace / Directory: search-bar hero as the primary CTA, category row, featured listings strip, trust section (features), testimonials, pricing, closing CTA
design_direction.motion_vocab: Stickers press on: scale from 1.15 to 1 with a 2deg rotate settle on reveal and on star-picker click, 200ms ease-out. Red-pen ellipses draw in via stroke-dashoffset once on entering the viewport. Cards lift 2px with the hard shadow growing to 5px on hover. All gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Typographic hero on the ruled worksheet: large Young Serif headline set on the blue baselines, the word 'only' circled in red pen. Below it a Yelp-style two-field search bar ('Find: dim sum, Thanksgiving, road trips' / 'Near: me, specifically') with a red search button. To the right on desktop, a small stack of three rotated index-card review previews with gold sticker ratings. No hero photo.
